correctness.rationale: The local product expansion yields a centered commutator h^2 K/2 plus O(h^3) uniformly; a noncommutative subset expansion controls all multi-perturbation effects by O(h^2) globally, negligible under h^(-3/2) scaling. Independent Rademacher triangular-array CLT proves the full covariance and centered Gaussian limit. Orthogonality of centered summands and Cauchy–Schwarz give exact limiting second moment. Invertibility gives positive constant iff K is nonzero, and the oscillator constant is computed exactly as 1/2. The standalone exact finite-grid second-moment verifier passed all seven tests and local symbolic coefficient tests; it is not used as an infinite-n proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A generic concentration upper bound—even if it yields an order in an adapted case—cannot yield an exact nonzero limit or full covariance without additional equalities; no stronger source currently inspected implies all of them. value.rationale: It resolves the natural question whether second-order ensemble error of random-order Lie products reflects single-run accuracy. It does not: exact h^(3/2) Gaussian path fluctuations have a computable nonzero commutator-controlled risk, with a sharp if-and-only-if commutation boundary; this provides an actionable error diagnostic for a canonical integrator across arbitrary fixed matrix dimensions.
